subject: How to save posterior iterations portion by portion?

messages.author: 614b5e0181ba03ae
messages.subject: How to save posterior iterations portion by portion?
parts:
Hi all,
May I know if there's an equivalent function in nimble to save the chain of iteration portion and keep on producing more iterations? Like the jags function "update()"? In jags, I have something like below:
## the jags model first
mod <- jags(data, parameters.to.save, model.file, n.chains, n.iter)
model.update <- mod
save(model.update)
  
  #--- update MCMC ----------
    for (i in 2:N.STEPS) {      
      
      model.update <- update(model.update,
                             parameters.to.save, n.iter)
      save(model.update)      
    }#end of i loop (steps)

The code above updates MCMC and save some iterations at multiple times.

Thanks.
Fengqing

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: How to save posterior iterations portion by portion?
parts:
Yes, assuming you have a compiled MCMC algorithm called "Cmcmc", you can continue running it to produce more iterations using the argument "reset = FALSE".  For example:

> Cmcmc$run(10000)   ## run for initial 10,000 iterations
> samples <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)   ## extract matrix of first 10,000 samples
> 
> Cmcmc$run(50000, reset=FALSE)      ## continue running the MCMC for an additional 50,000 iterations
> samples60 <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)   ## extract matrix of all 60,000 samples
> 

Hope that helps!

messages.subject: Re: How to save posterior iterations portion by portion?
parts:
Hi Daniel,
Thanks for your help!

It seems to me that the Cmcmc will become bigger and bigger when I continue to run more iterations. Sometimes I need a very long burnin for my model to get converge. The machine will run out of space/memory to continue the run since Cmcmc will become too big. Is there a way to get by this?


I need at lease 1 million iterations to get convergent, with about 5k parameters. I'm not sure when my model will converge. So I need to let the mcmc run for 2 or 3 millions and monitor the iterations from time to time. I'm wondering if nimble can discard the past iterations (to free up the space) after I save each portion of iterations and keep on running the mcmc (like what jags did as shown in the code in my 1st post)?


Thanks!

Fengqing

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: How to save posterior iterations portion by portion?
parts:
Fengquing, there's no immediate muilt-in mechanism to do what you're asking: to stop recording samples, then start recording samples at a later point.   The best built-in approach would be to use the option for thinning the samples, which would only record every 100th or 1000th sample (the frequency is up to you).  To specify the MCMC to only record every 1000th sample (of all the parameters), you would set the thinning interval using the MCMC configuration object as:

> conf$setThin(1000)

Then proceed to build the MCMC algorithm from the conf object, compile it, and run it:

> Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
> Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, ...)
> Cmcmc$run(...)

There are other options for what you're trying to do, which would require some custom NIMBLE code, but could certainly be done.  I'll followup with you about other possibilities, too.

Keep in touch,
Daniel
